sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Short title, extent and commencement

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.--(1) This Act may be called the Punjab Supervision and
Control of Children Homes Act, 1976.
(2) It extends to the whole of
the Punjab.
(3) It shall come into force on
such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette,
appoint in this behalf.

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Definitions

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
2. Definitions.--In this
Act, unless the context otherwise requires:‑
(a)
"Board" means Board constituted under Section 3 of this Act;
(b)
"Chairman" means the Chairman of the Board;
(c)
"Children Home" means a building, structure or enclosure or any
institution or part thereof which is used for the reception, maintenance and
care of orphans;
(d)
"Government" means the Government of the Punjab;
(e)
"Governing Body" means a person or group of persons responsible for
the management and control of a Children Home;
(f)
"Licensing Authority" means the Director, Social Welfare Punjab or
any other officer appointed or nominated by him to be a Licensing Authority for,
the purposes of this Act;
(g) "member" means a member of the Board;
(h) "orphan" means any child under the age of eighteen years
who:‑
(i) has lost his parents or one of
the parents and has no adequate source of income;
(ii) or is unclaimed; or
(iii) has parents who are destitutes
or who has been deserted by his parents;
(i) "Prescribed" means prescribed by rules;
(j)
"Secretary" means the Secretary of the Board;
(k) "rules" means the rules made under this Act; and
(l)
"Voluntary Social Welfare Agency" means an organisation,
association or undertaking established by a person or group of persons for
rendering welfare services and depending for its resources on public
subscriptions, donations or Government aid and registered under the Voluntary
Social Welfare Agencies (Registration and Control) Ordinance, 1961.

Punjab Board for the Supervision and Control of Children Homes."

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Membership of the Board

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]

An Act to provide

4. Membership of the Board.--(1)
The Board shall consist of a Chairman and the following members:‑
(a) Minister for
Finance, Punjab.
(b) Minister for
Auqaf, Punjab.
(c) Minister for
Education, Punjab.
(d) One
representative of Chamber of Commerce and Industry to be nominated by the
Government.
(e) Secretary to
Government of the Punjab, Finance Department.
(f) Secretary to
Government of the Punjab, Auqaf
Department.
(g) Secretary to
Government of the Punjab, Education
Department.
(h) Secretary to
Government of the Punjab, Social Welfare
Department.
(i) Director, Social Welfare, Government of the Punjab.
(j) five improvement social workers or philanthropists to be
nominated by the Chairman; and
(k) five members of the Provincial Assembly of the Punjab, one from each Division to be elected by the
Assembly.
(2) The Minister incharge of Social Welfare
Department shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Board.
(3) The Director Social Welfare
shall be the ex-officio Secretary of the Board.
(4) The Chairman shall, on the
recommendation of the Secretary, nominate five prominent social workers and
philanthropists mentioned in clause (1) of sub‑section (1).

5. Temporary Vacancies.--If
for any reason, the Chairman becomes unable to perform his duties temporarily,
Government shall nominate any other member to act as Chairman till such time

(2) In case office of the
Secretary falls temporarily vacant, the Government may nominate any other
member of the Board to perform the duties of the Secretary during the

9. Functionaries of the Board
to be public servants.--The members of the Board, its employees and every
person empowered by the Board to exercise any of its powers under this Act,
shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the
Pakistan Penal Code.

10. Delegation of powers.--(1)

powers and functions to them as it may deem necessary,

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976

Fund

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.

[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide

11. Fund.--(1) There shall
be a fund of the Board called the Punjab Children Homes Funds.
(2) The Fund shall consist of:‑
(a) all money received by the Board from the Government, Federal
Government or any other agency;
(b) all money collected through zakat,
fitra, donations, charities and, other contributions;
(c) all money received or collected under this Act as fee, etc.;
and
(d) all money raised by the Board from the banks or any other
agency as loans:
Provided that Zakat shall be spent in
accordance with the Injunctions of the Holy Quran and
the Sunnah. of the Holy Prophet as enunciated
in the Zakat and Ushr
Ordinance, 1980 QCVII of 1980) or any other law for the time begin in force and
fitra shall be spent in accordance with the said
Injunctions.

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Functions of the Board

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
13. Functions of the Board.--The
functions of the Board shall be:-
(a) to formulate policies with regard to the objectives of the
Board;
(b) to plan, coordinate, integrate, evaluate and encourage
welfare services for orphans in the Punjab;
(c) to supervise and regulate the working of Children Homes by
giving them professional, technical and financial assistance;
(d) to perform any other functions entrusted to it by or under
any law;
(e) to control the rising and utilization of funds by executive
body of Children Homes and to arrange for their audit;
(f) to raise the educational and moral standard in the Children
Homes;
(g) to introduce industrial and technical training for the
orphans; and
(h) to arrange the scholarships for higher education of the
orphans.

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Prohibition to establish or continue a Children Home without a licence

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
14. Prohibition to establish
or continue a Children Home without a licence.--No
person or a voluntary social welfare agency shall establish or continue a
Children Home except under a licence issued by the
Licensing Authority:
Provided that a
person or a voluntary social welfare agency continuing a Children Home on the
date of commencement of this Act may obtain a licence
within thirty days of the said date:
Provided further that all the orphanages existing on the date of
commencement of this Act shall be called as Children Homes.

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Separate Children Homes for males and females

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
15. Separate Children Homes
for males and females.--(1) There shall be separate Children Homes for
males and females.
(2) A person or a voluntary
social welfare agency applying for a licence to run a
Children Home shall mention in the application whether the Children Home for which
the licence is required, is male or female Children
Home.

Issue of a licence

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
16. Issue of a licence.--On receipt of an application for issue of a licence in the prescribed form along with a fee at the rate
of Rs. 50 per Children Home, the Licensing Authority
shall hold inquiry to find justification for the opening or continuance of a
Children Home and may issue a licence on such terms
and conditions as may be prescribed:
Provided that no male person shall be issued a licence
for returning a Children Home for female orphans.

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Renewal, suspension or cancellation of licence

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
17. Renewal, suspension or
cancellation of licence.--A licence
issued under Section 16:-
(i) shall be valid for a period of
two years from the date of its issue;
(ii) may when an
application is made on the prescribed form within a week of the date of expiry
of the licence be renewed by the Licensing Authority
without fee for a further period not exceeding two years at a time; and
(iii) may after giving the licence an
opportunity of being heard, be suspended or cancelled by the Licensing
Authority, if there is contravention of any of the provisions of this Act or
any breach of the conditions of the licence.

19. Medical Examination of
orphans.--The Governing body of a Children Home shall have every orphan
admitted into the Children Home medically examined within seven days of such
admission and thereafter shall have to continue such practice once a year and
keep a record to this effect in the prescribed form.

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Prevention of begging

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
20. Prevention of begging.--The
Governing body of a Children Home shall in no circumstances allow or cause an
orphan admitted into a Children Home to beg for alms or solicit for donations
or subscriptions in any way or form; nor shall such -an orphan be made or permitted
to act in any manner incompatible with human dignity.

21. Penalties.--Whoever
contravenes any provisions of this Act shall be punished with a rigorous
imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years but which shall not be
less than one year, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or
with both.

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Maintenance and inspection of accounts

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
22. Maintenance and inspection
of accounts.--(1) The Governing body of a Children Home shall maintain or
cause to be maintained accounts of income and expenditure of the Children Home
in the manner prescribed.
(2) The Board or any person authorised by it in this behalf may inspect the accounts of
a Children Home and issue such Directions as it may deem necessary and the
Governing Body shall carry out such directions.
(3) The Governing Body of a
Children Home shall be bound to produce or cause to be produced its record
before the Board or the Licensing Authority or its nominee as and when
required.

sections.shortTitle: The Punjab Supervision Control of Children Home Act 1976
sections.description:
Power to make rules

THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
THE PUNJAB SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OF CHILDREN HOME ACT, 1976
[PB.
ACT NO. XVI OF 1976]
[16th November, 1976]
An Act to provide
for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate
the working and control of Children Homes in the Punjab
24. Power to make rules.--(1)
Subject to the provisions of this Act and with the approval of the Government
the Board may make rules, for the purpose of carrying into effect the
provisions of this Act.
(2) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power such rules may provide for
all or any of the following matters, namely:-
(a) the procedure to be followed at the meeting of the Board;
(b) the terms and conditions of service of the employees of the
Board;
(c) the powers and duties of the Chairman, Secretary and the
members of the Board;
(d) the form of Application for issue or renewal of licences;
(e) the form and conditions on which licences
may be issued;
(f) the form of making reports of medical examination and
admission of orphans; and
(g) any other matter which may be considered necessary for
carrying out the purposes of this Act.
